metadata.title: The Monday Brief Isn't Memory.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: does Claude already know your numbers every Monday, or does it check them? Lands the carry-out that it checks against a written file that says exactly what counts, and returns exactly that, every time.
metadata.anchor_pair: N/A — source is skill-teardown format (anatomy -> pipeline -> constraint -> verdict), no anchor structure to preserve

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes Claude already knows their numbers every Monday, like it's memorized the business. It doesn't. It checks — reading a written file that spells out exactly what a Monday brief means here.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Does Claude just know my numbers on Monday?', hesitates on 'know', corrects to 'check'

beats.act: 1 anatomy — a skill is a file
beats.narration_text: This kind of briefing runs from something called a skill — a single file, written in plain language, that Claude reads before it starts. It isn't pulling from memory. It's following the file. The file is the whole program.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder icon opening to reveal one file, SKILL.md, highlighted, captioned '1 file total'

production_viz.label: A skill is one file
production_viz.mechanic: A folder opens on cream to reveal a single item: SKILL.md (highlighted in crimson), captioned '1 file total.' A caption below reads 'Claude reads it, then follows it.'

beats.narration_text: The steps run in a fixed order: read the file, work through each step exactly as written, then hand back the result. Nothing runs out of sequence unless a step itself says so.

shot.new_visual_element: Three-phase pipeline: Read SKILL.md -> Execute each step in order -> Return output

production_viz.label: Input in, output out
production_viz.mechanic: Three cards left to right joined by arrows: 'Read SKILL.md', 'Execute each step in order', 'Return output'. Linear, no branch points drawn.

beats.act: 3 constraint — what belongs on the page
beats.narration_text: For this skill, the file specifies exactly what belongs on the page: cash, sales, and pipeline; the week ahead; and your top three to-dos. It can also take where to post the result, or where to save it. Ask for anything the file doesn't list, and there's no step that covers it.

shot.new_visual_element: Three checklist rows filling in; a boundary line with 'plus where to post it, or save it — nothing else' beyond

production_viz.label: Exactly what belongs on the page
production_viz.mechanic: Three rows fill in one at a time with a checkmark: 'Cash, sales, and pipeline', 'The week ahead', 'Top three to-dos'. A dashed boundary line beneath the list, with a faint caption below it: 'plus where to post it, or save it — nothing else'.

beats.narration_text: Claude doesn't already know your Monday numbers — it checks them, against a written file that says exactly what counts, and returns exactly that, the same way every time.

props.quote: Claude doesn't already know your Monday numbers — it checks them, against a written file that says exactly what counts, and returns exactly that, the same way every time.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Pull together a one-page Monday brief for me: cash and sales, what's moving in the pipeline, what's on deck this week, and my top three to-dos. Tell me if anything's missing that you'd need from me first. Liam, in for Bear.
